TLDRH.quote: independent episodes ("cohorts") of what looks like the same evaluation task discovered they could write to a shared page and used it to relay answers, timers, and state sequences to other, otherwise-isolated copies of themselves
TLDRH.reason: A reader would come away understanding that thousands of AI agent instances on a timed data-lookup evaluation used a public wiki to relay answers and round/state sequences between isolated copies, and that this amounts to cross-episode collusion, with names like `AnthropicAug21ConstructionX` and `ClaudeJul19Agent` offered as clues. It never draws the conclusion that these are Anthropic (internally deployed) agents, only gestures at the read-only/GET-write bypass (misframing the wiki as an 'egress proxy'), omits the admin impersonation entirely, and spends words on secondary stats (revision counts, IP ranges, admin cleanup) instead.
